Corrections: ListenerProbeRemote is used by three test files, not one (app_host_deploy_e2e_test.go:806,859; app_host_deploy_safety_test.go:317,324; app_host_pipeline_container_e2e_test.go:911). restartBare/stopAndRelaunch are defined only in legacy_restart_test.go (144 lines, zero Test funcs), so that whole file is a test-only reimplementation of the dead path. setPendingRestart/Start have 15 test references across 7 test files; version_test.go is 3,811 lines.

Needs Jesse's go-ahead (deletes implementations).

title: Attach/publish/announce state machine implemented three times (Ensure, AttachUnderGate, reconnectOnce)
note: Structure confirmed: Ensure (manager.go:553-825), AttachUnderGate (:916-1033), reconnectOnce (:2766-2863) each run ensureOnce -> isClosed/isLost -> SameRegistration recheck (:739,:999,:2803) -> publishChannel -> afterPublish -> second death check -> detach/attach events; the baseCtx.Err()!=nil && !isTerminal -> ErrManagerClosed mapping is pasted at :628-ish, :970, :2840. Ensure has 16 lock.Unlock() and 8 ch.Close() calls in 270 lines. Overstated as pure duplication though: the tails differ for real reasons. reconnectOnce owns the host (defer Unlock, closes the channel under the lock, clearChannel on lost-after-publish and returns true to retry); Ensure/AttachUnderGate give the slot back to the predecessor via lostAfterPublish (:1170) and close outside the lock; AttachUnderGate runs under the caller's hold and closes stale itself. Ensure also has the extra post-startSupervise checks the others lack. A single helper with an outcome enum must encode those differences, so the -150..-250 net estimate is optimistic (I expect -60 to -120) and concurrency risk is real.
revised_fix_plan: Extract only the genuinely identical pieces first: mapAttemptErr(ctx,err) for the Close-vs-terminal mapping, and a validatePublishable(name,host,ch) (closed/lost/SameRegistration) helper returning a small reason enum. Leave each caller's tail policy inline. Add a table test per outcome before touching Ensure. Do after finding 1 and as its own PR; reconsider the full publishAttached helper only if the small extraction leaves obvious residue.

title: ensureOnce is a 351-line ladder and operations.go re-implements its deploy and restart legs

Deploy leg respelled in operations.go:145-181 (deploySelectedWithSupersession, acknowledgeDeployment, setResolvedTarget, reReadLaunchContract, deployedBuildNotStamped, clearPendingRestart) vs manager.go:2037-2092. Correction: finishEnsureOp has 6 call sites (manager.go:2051,2075,2081,2090,2153,2158), 15 mentions; the 'if finishEnsureOp != nil' guards inside the deploy block are redundant since the hook's finish was just assigned. The restart leg in restartForOperation (operations.go:253-376) actually twins restartHubWithStartProof (version.go:532-556: prepareSelectedRestart, store pending under m.mu, restartPreparedSelectedPending) more than ensureOnce itself. Possible latent defect worth a test, not proven: when deploy and restart are both planned, validateStartupContract / validateExecutable failures (manager.go:~2095-2105) return without calling finishEnsureOp, leaving the durable record open.
revised_fix_plan: Split ensureOnce into named phases and make DeployForOperation/restartForOperation call the same runDeployLeg/runRestartLeg, using a deferred finish with a named return instead of 6 inline guarded calls. Also fold restartHubWithStartProof's prepare+store block and restartForOperation's into one prepareAndStoreRestart. Start with a red test for the open-record-on-validation-failure case to decide whether it is a bug. Sequence after findings 1, 9, 10; size -150 to -300.
